description: European Grid Capacity Maps is an interactive open-access tool, created by Maarten Staats, a Dutch grid operator employee, as a personal project, that gathers the sources showing available electricity grid capacity across Europe. For each region it links to the official data sources and grid operators, in three views: supply (capacity to connect generation), demand (capacity to connect load) and a simplified view. Coverage: European countries and regions for which capacity maps were found; the list was not read because the site is built with scripts. The notes explain that capacity maps show remaining space on the grid, calculated by operators from current use, planned connections and expected growth, that some regions show transmission (TSO) capacity and others distribution (DSO) capacity or both, and that formats range from colour coding to raw numbers. Format and access: an interactive map and a configurable download of capacity data for all regions, with optional metadata; free. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the author calls it a starting point for exploring sources, not a complete solution; information was gathered through search engines, social media and limited contact with operators, so values are for indication only and must be checked with the operators. Simulation uses: screening where new generation, storage or electrified demand can connect, for capacity planning of distribution and transmission grids. Related records: the E-REDES open data portal (data-e-redes-open-data-portal) is one operator source of hosting capacity.
